name: alert
title: Alert
description: An inline message about the page or a section of it, in one of five tones.

examples.name: alert-demo
examples.title: Alert
examples.description: An info alert and a neutral one.

examples.name: alert-tones
examples.title: Tones
examples.description: Neutral, info, success, warning and danger. Each tone has its own icon, so colour is never the only signal.

examples.name: alert-with-action
examples.title: Actions, dismiss and live
examples.description: A button or link in the action slot, a dismissible alert, and a live alert without an icon.

props.name: title
props.description: Short summary shown in semibold above the body.

props.name: children
props.description: The message body. Links inside are underlined in the tone colour.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the tone glyph inside the tone chip. `false` shows no icon.

props.name: action
props.description: A small Button or a link. Sits at the inline end, and wraps under the text when the alert is narrow.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a close button that calls this. You remove the alert.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the close button.

props.name: live
props.description: Announce the alert when it appears: `true`/'assertive' → role="alert", 'polite' → role="status". Leave unset for alerts present on page load.

keyboard.action: Moves to the action and the close button, in reading order.
Activates the focused close button or action.

notes: No live role by default, so alerts rendered with the page are not re-announced. Set `live` for alerts that appear after a user action (e.g. a failed submit).
With `live`, the alert is named by its title (aria-labelledby).
Every tone has a distinct icon plus a text title; colour is never the only signal.
The close button is a 24×24px target (WCAG 2.5.8) and has an accessible name.

do: Lead with what happened, then what to do next.
Use danger for problems that block the task; warning for things that will become problems.
Keep the action to one short verb phrase.
dont: Don't use an alert for transient confirmations — use a toast.
Don't set `live` on alerts that are present when the page loads.
Don't stack several alerts of the same tone; combine them.
